description.narrative: The impact of the war in Gaza has transcended geographical boundaries, casting a shadow over the West Bank. The Israeli market lockdown, implemented as a response to the emergency conditions in Israel, has severed critical economic lifelines, leaving a substantial portion of the Palestinian workers unemployed. This has resulted in a cascading effect on the affordability of essential food items, amplifying the originally existing challenges faced by communities. Compounding the economic strain, the Palestinian Authority's inability to disburse partial salaries for almost 50 days has exacerbated financial hardships in addition to the complicated fundingchallenges that are faced by the main humanitarian stakeholder in the camps (UNRWA) that have led to reduction of the main servicesand support that were provided by the agency. The combined effect of these challenges has created a large segment of the populationwithout income, rendering them vulnerable and deepening the cycle of poverty. Finally, the recent Israeli military campaigns and settler violence in West Bank and especially in Tulkarem, Jenin and Tubas refugee camps have further marginalized Palestinian residents, particularly in the targeted refugee camps in Tulkarem governorate, hindering their food security and basic nutrition. PARC idea can be summarized by the following: PARC will distribute food parcels containing the main dry food items common in the Palestinian houses that are identified by the food security cluster (FSS Cluster) in cooperation with the NGOs and INGOs in Palestine. These parcels will target approximately 1500 Households (one parcel per HH), that are facing difficult circumstances resulted by the recent and continuous Israeli military campaign inside and around these refugee camps in Tulkarem.

participating-org.narrative: In 1983 a small group of agronomists founded the Palestinian Agricultural Relief Committees (PARC), which has since developed into one of the most important Palestinian non-governmental organisations providing services to poor and marginalised farmers onthe West Bank and Gaza Strip, working to make agricultural businesses grow. PARC#s goal is to promote an economic and social climate that would allow the Palestinian agricultural sector to develop sustainably. Another goal is to improve the living standard of Palestinians living in rural areas, especially of poor farming families. PARC provides a broad range of agricultural extension services. It is active in land reclamation and in building rural access roads. The organisation advocates the improvementof rural women#s economic position. It is part of an Oxfam Novib-funded three-year gender-focus program. In 1991 PARC got an ISO-certification. It was the first and so far only non-governmental organisation in the Arab world to obtain one. It has also developed an impressive strategic ten-year plan for the 1998-2008 period. Together with several other agricultural non-governmental organisations (NGOs) PARC has signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the Ministry of Agriculture, which sees PARC#s workasindependent and complementary to its own. PARC is active in a network of Palestinian NGOs and a member of the governing committee of the Palestinian NGO-network. Oxfam Novib has been supporting PARC since 1982. In 1999 Oxfam Novib, ICCO, Christian Aid (UK) and Oxfam Great Britain set up a donor consortium to support PARC. This provides PARC a measure of long-term financial security. It also makes technical and organisational assistance available to PARC in further developing its program.
